chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Fazl al-Nawfali, from Ibn Abu Yahya al-Razi, who said:
Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not mix with, nor have dealings with, anyone except the one who grew up in goodness.'

key_terms.تُخَالِطُوا: to mix with or associate closely

ai.seo_question: Who should Muslims associate with according to hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the principle of *al-mu'asharah* (social companionship), advising believers to limit their interactions to those whose upbringing (*tarbiyah*) in goodness ensures moral consistency. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *al-khayr* (goodness) as an intrinsic quality cultivated from youth, serving as a reliable predictor of character in both social and commercial contexts. The instruction underscores the importance of selective association (*khilat*) to preserve spiritual and ethical integrity within the community.
